</details>

<details>
<summary>🎛 Adaptive per-shard rerank (ADR-155 §6)</summary>

Under federation, RaBitQ would run its `rerank_factor × k` rerank once per shard, costing K× more work as shard count grows. ruLake divides the budget:

```
per_shard_rerank = max(MIN_PER_SHARD_RERANK, global_rerank / K)
```

K=4 at rerank×20 → 5 per shard. Measured recall@10 stays above 85 % (gate test). Callers needing byte-exact single-shard parity use `search_federated_with_rerank(.., Some(global_rerank))`.

</details>

<details>
<summary>⚡ Arc-based concurrency (the 13.2× win)</summary>

`CacheEntry::index` is `Arc<RabitqPlusIndex>`. Readers:

1. Lock cache mutex
2. Clone the Arc (refcount bump — cycles, not milliseconds)
3. **Drop the lock**
4. Scan without holding anything shared

Index is immutable after build, so concurrent scans are a pure data race against nothing. This is the single biggest performance win on the branch — **8-12× concurrent QPS**.

</details>

## User guide

<details>
<summary>🎚 Choose a consistency mode</summary>

| Symptom / requirement | Mode |
|---|---|
| Legal / compliance — can't serve stale data, ever | `Fresh` |
| Search, RAG, recommendation, agent retrieval | `Eventual { ttl_ms: 60_000 }` |
| Audit snapshot — data is cryptographically pinned | `Frozen` |

</details>

<details>
<summary>📏 Size the cache</summary>

```rust
// Unbounded — fine for small collections
let lake = RuLake::new(20, 42);

// LRU-capped for memory-bounded serving processes
let lake = RuLake::new(20, 42).with_max_cache_entries(100);
```

Only unpinned entries (refcount == 0) are evicted; active `(backend, collection)` pointers keep their entry alive.

</details>

<details>
<summary>📊 Operational metrics</summary>

| Metric | Signal | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `hit_rate` | < 0.95 | Grow cache or warm aggressively |
| `last_prime_ms` | spiking | Backend RTT changed or collection grew |
| `primes` | growing unexpectedly | Check for witness churn |
| `shared_hits` | > 0 | Cross-backend sharing is working |
| `invalidations` | climbing | Coherence protocol firing — inspect |
| `warm_installs` | > 0 | `warm_from_dir` is being used |

Per-backend and per-collection views via `cache_stats_by_backend()` / `cache_stats_by_collection()`.

</details>

<details>
<summary>🚀 Run the examples</summary>

```bash
# End-to-end sidecar daemon (publisher + reader + coherence loop)
cargo run --release -p rulake --example sidecar_daemon

# Save → ship → warm-restart cycle
cargo run --release -p rulake --example warm_restart

# Benchmark harness (~2 minutes)
cargo run --release -p rulake --bin rulake-demo

# Fast mode (~5 seconds, just n=5k)
cargo run --release -p rulake --bin rulake-demo -- --fast

## Comparison with other systems

| System           | Intermediary tax | Cross-backend federation | Witness-authenticated | Cross-process cache sharing | CPU-first / GPU-optional | `unsafe` count |
|------------------|-----------------:|-------------------------:|----------------------:|----------------------------:|-------------------------:|---------------:|
| **ruLake**       | **1.02×**        | ✅ (rayon fan-out)       | ✅ (SHAKE‑256)         | ✅ (content-addressed)      | ✅                       | **0**          |
| Pinecone         | n/a (hosted)     | ❌                        | ❌                    | ❌                          | n/a                      | n/a            |
| Weaviate         | n/a (hosted)     | ❌                        | ❌                    | ❌                          | ✅                       | n/a            |
| Milvus           | ~1.5–2×          | partial                   | ❌                    | ❌                          | ✅                       | many           |
| LanceDB          | ~1.1–1.3×        | ❌                        | ❌                    | ❌                          | ✅                       | some           |
| BQ Vector Search | n/a (hosted)     | ❌ (BQ-only)              | ❌                    | ❌                          | n/a                      | n/a            |
| QVCache (2026)   | region-adaptive  | ❌                        | ❌                    | ❌                          | ✅                       | unknown        |

ruLake is explicitly **not** a vector database — it doesn't own storage. It's the substrate that lets you query whichever vector DB or lakehouse you already have, with a coherent compression + governance story across all of them.

Rust crate / manifest: ruvector-rulake-gcs
Path: crates/gcs-backend/Cargo.toml
Description: GCS Parquet BackendAdapter for ruLake (ADR-155 §M2)

# ruLake GCS backend — Parquet-on-GCS BackendAdapter (ADR-155 §M2).
#
# Implements `BackendAdapter` for Parquet vector files stored on
# Google Cloud Storage. Generation = GCS object generation number
# (`Generation::Num`) so cache coherence rides the existing GCS
# atomicity guarantees — every successful upload bumps the gen.
#
# Standalone Cargo package per ADR-001 (no root workspace).
#
# Build:  cargo build --release
# Test:   cargo test --release         (offline; smoke against fixtures)
#         RULAKE_GCS_LIVE_TEST=1 \
#         RULAKE_GCS_BUCKET=ruv-rulake-test cargo test --release -- --ignored
#                                       (live; needs gcloud ADC)

[package]
name = "ruvector-rulake-gcs"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"
license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"
authors = ["Ruvector Team"]
repository = "https://github.com/ruvnet/RuLake"
description = "GCS Parquet BackendAdapter for ruLake (ADR-155 §M2)"

[dependencies]
rulake = { path = "../core", version = "2.3.0-alpha.1" }

# Unified storage abstraction. The `gcp` feature pulls in the GCS
# transport (which honours gcloud Application Default Credentials).
# `tokio` feature lets us use the async API; we wrap it in a blocking
# bridge so the BackendAdapter trait (sync) stays satisfied.
object_store = { version = "0.13", default-features = false, features = ["gcp"] }

# Apache Parquet reader. `arrow` feature gets us the RecordBatch API
# we use for vector decoding.
parquet = { version = "58", default-features = false, features = ["arrow", "snap", "zstd", "async", "object_store"] }
arrow = { version = "58", default-features = false, features = ["prettyprint"] }

# Async runtime — only used inside the blocking bridge wrapping
# object_store / parquet's async APIs. Single-threaded current-thread
# runtime keeps the dep tree light.
tokio = { version = "1.39", default-features = false, features = ["rt", "macros"] }

# Streaming + futures glue for async parquet reads.
futures = "0.3"
bytes = "1"

# Errors. anyhow at the boundary; structured errors map back to
# `RuLakeError::Backend { backend, detail }` in the trait impl.
anyhow = "1"

# Logging.
tracing = "0.1"

[dev-dependencies]
tempfile = "3"
tokio = { version = "1.39", features = ["rt-multi-thread", "macros"] }
criterion = { version = "0.5", features = ["html_reports"] }

[[bench]]
name    = "pull_vectors"
harness = false

[profile.release]
opt-level = 3
lto = "thin"
codegen-units = 1
strip = "symbols"
title: ruvector-rulake-gcs

Rust crate / manifest: ruvector-rulake-ipfs
Path: crates/ipfs-backend/Cargo.toml
Description: IPFS BackendAdapter for ruLake — bundle distribution + content addressing (ADR-005)

# ruLake IPFS backend — bundle distribution over IPFS (ADR-005).
#
# Stores `table.rulake.json` bundles on IPFS and addresses them by
# CID. Vector bodies stay on the original backend (Parquet/GCS/etc.);
# this layer is the bundle/witness distribution plane only.
#
# Standalone Cargo package per ADR-001 (no root workspace).
#
# Build:  cargo build --release
# Test:   cargo test --release                    (4 offline tests)
#         RULAKE_IPFS_LIVE_TEST=1 \
#         RULAKE_IPFS_KUBO_API=http://127.0.0.1:5001 \
#         cargo test --release -- --ignored ipfs_live

[package]
name = "ruvector-rulake-ipfs"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"
license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"
authors = ["Ruvector Team"]
repository = "https://github.com/ruvnet/RuLake"
description = "IPFS BackendAdapter for ruLake — bundle distribution + content addressing (ADR-005)"

[dependencies]
rulake = { path = "../core", version = "2.3.0-alpha.1" }

# Note: we deliberately don't use `ipfs-api-backend-hyper` for v0.1.
# It transitively pulls multihash 0.17 → core2 0.4 (yanked). Kubo's
# HTTP RPC is just `POST /api/v0/{add,cat,pin/add}` with simple JSON
# responses — talking to it via `reqwest` directly is ~50 LOC and
# cuts ~40 transitive dependencies. A higher-level SDK can land in
# v0.2 once the upstream multihash chain unyanks.
#
# We also don't pull the `cid` crate — same yanked transitive. CIDs
# are passed as opaque strings; kubo and the gateway canonically
# validate them on the wire.

# Async runtime for the kubo HTTP calls. Wrapped in a current-thread
# blocking bridge so the sync BackendAdapter trait stays satisfied
# (same pattern as gcs-backend).
tokio = { version = "1.39", default-features = false, features = ["rt", "macros"] }
futures = "0.3"
bytes = "1"

# HTTP client — the kubo HTTP RPC endpoint AND the public-gateway
# fallback (Mode::Gateway / Mode::KuboWithGatewayFallback). One client
# library, two endpoints. `multipart` is needed for `POST /api/v0/add`
# which requires a multipart body per the kubo RPC spec.
reqwest = { version = "0.12", default-features = false, features = ["rustls-tls", "json", "stream", "multipart"] }

anyhow = "1"
tracing = "0.1"
serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1"

[dev-dependencies]
tempfile = "3"
tokio = { version = "1.39", features = ["rt-multi-thread", "macros", "net"] }
# Mock kubo HTTP server for offline tests.
hyper = { version = "1", features = ["server", "http1"] }
hyper-util = { version = "0.1", features = ["tokio", "server-auto", "service"] }
http-body-util = "0.1"
criterion = { version = "0.5", features = ["html_reports"] }

[[bench]]
name    = "verify_bundle"
harness = false

[profile.release]
opt-level = 3
lto = "thin"
codegen-units = 1
strip = "symbols"
title: ruvector-rulake-ipfs

Description: AVX-512 VectorKernel impl for ruLake (ADR-157)

# ruLake AVX-512 kernel — SIMD impl of the ADR-157 `VectorKernel` trait.
#
# This crate provides an `Avx512Kernel` that uses x86_64 AVX-512

Rust crate / manifest: ruvector-rulake-mcp-ruqu
Path: crates/mcp-ruqu/Cargo.toml
Description: MCP companion server for ruQu v2 — agent-callable, witness-aware quantum execution surface (ADR-008 §6)

# ruQu MCP companion server (ADR-008 §6 v0.1).
#
# v0.0.1 shipped the five tools (rmcp `#[tool_router]` pattern):
#   * `ruqu_simulate`    (publish-tier — allocates Hilbert-space RAM)
#   * `ruqu_verify`      (read-tier   — replays + byte-equal witness check)
#   * `ruqu_replay`      (read-tier   — cache short-circuit via lake.search_one)
#   * `ruqu_optimize`    (read-tier   — stub; planner ships in v0.2)
#   * `ruqu_qec_schedule`(read-tier   — stub; QEC ships in v0.2)
# plus JSONL audit, R-1 / R-2 / R-3 mitigations, stdio transport.
#
# v0.1 adds (this release):
#   - Streamable HTTP transport, lifted near-verbatim from
#     `mcp-rvdna::http` (commit a66d65f) — same iter 32 CORS layer
#     (echo Origin, expose `mcp-session-id`, short-circuit OPTIONS
#     preflight). Default bind 127.0.0.1:7442 (avoids clash with
#     rvdna-mcp's documented 7441 default).
#   - `ruqu-mcp` binary with `stdio` / `http` subcommands matching
#     `rvdna-mcp`'s CLI shape so a single operator script can drive
#     both servers.
#   - JSONL `--audit-file` sink (was stderr-only in v0.0.1).
#
# Out of scope for v0.1 (deferred to mcp-ruqu v0.2):
#   - mTLS, JWT/JWKS, rate limiting, replay guard. The HTTP `serve()`
#     signature already carries the `AuthMode` / `BearerAuth` /
#     `AllowBearerOnPublic` / `InsecureAllowNoAuth` types so the
#     v0.2 lift from `mcp-server::http` is mechanical.
#   - The `simulate` / `hardware` / `verify` capability tier additions
#     from ADR-008 §6 Decision 4 — capability set is plumbed but the
#     v0.1 tools still gate on the existing `Read` / `Publish` tiers
#     so we don't fork the policy module before mcp-server agrees.
#
# Standalone Cargo package per ADR-001 (no root workspace; sibling
# crates reach each other via path-deps; rulake from crates.io v2.2).

[package]
name        = "ruvector-rulake-mcp-ruqu"
version     = "0.1.0"
edition     = "2021"
rust-version = "1.89"
license     = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"
authors     = ["Ruvector Team"]
repository  = "https://github.com/ruvnet/RuLake"
description = "MCP companion server for ruQu v2 — agent-callable, witness-aware quantum execution surface (ADR-008 §6)"

[[bin]]
name = "ruqu-mcp"
path = "src/main.rs"

[dependencies]
# The v0.0.x stub substrate (StateVector / Stabilizer / TensorNetwork /
# Hardware-stub) — kept for the existing wire shape + witness semantics.

# v0.0.1 scope:
# - 5 read-tier tools: rvdna_find, rvdna_call_variants, rvdna_translate,
#   rvdna_score, rvdna_lineage. Only `rvdna_lineage` works end-to-end —
#   the other four return shaped stubs plus the live witness so callers
#   exercise the same wire path full impls will use.
# - Witness-pinned reads: every tool re-derives `current_bundle` against
#   the registered `RvdnaT0Backend` and refuses with `RVDNA_WITNESS_DRIFT`
#   when the cached lineage's witness disagrees (R-1 mitigation, per
#   docs/research/security/v0.0-substrates.md).

#   so operators can diff rvdna-side and rulake-side traces verbatim.
# - Capability gating (read|publish|admin|internal) but with the rvdna
#   scope vocabulary (`mcp:rvdna:read`, `mcp:rvdna:internal`, …).
# - Stdio + Streamable HTTP transports, mirroring mcp-server's surface.
# - Mutation surface is intentionally zero: NO put_collection / publish /
#   admin tools in v0.0.1. The operator wires `RvdnaT0Backend`s in at
#   process start; the wire surface is read-only.

# Standalone Cargo package per ADR-001 (no root workspace; rvdna-backend

text:
Rust crate / manifest: ruvector-rulake-mcp
Path: crates/mcp-server/Cargo.toml
Description: MCP server for ruLake — agent-callable, witness-aware vector cache (ADR-004)

# ruLake MCP server (ADR-004 v0.2).
#
# v0.2 scope:
# - stdio transport (carried forward from v0.1)
# - Streamable HTTP transport (--http :PORT)
# - bearer-token auth on the HTTP path (dev-only flag for public bind)
# - DNS-rebinding guard via rmcp's allowed_hosts (loopback by default)
# - one public tool: rulake_query (intent=search; verify/explain/refresh
#   land in later iterations)
# - LocalBackend + FsBackend backends from a config file
# - bounded worker pool via flume + rayon
# - JSONL audit log to stderr (file output deferred)
# - witness-fail-closed wherever bundles are touched
#
# Standalone Cargo package per ADR-001 (no root workspace; the parent
# rulake crate is reached via `path = ".."`).

[package]
name = "ruvector-rulake-mcp"
version = "0.8.0"
edition = "2021"
license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"
authors = ["Ruvector Team"]
repository = "https://github.com/ruvnet/RuLake"
description = "MCP server for ruLake — agent-callable, witness-aware vector cache (ADR-004)"

[[bin]]
name = "rulake-mcp"
path = "src/main.rs"

[dependencies]
# The ruLake crate the server wraps. Per ADR-001, sibling-crate path-dep.
# Pinned to the alpha (cargo refuses pre-release matches via plain
# major versions). When the root crate goes 2.3.0 stable, bump here.
rulake = { path = "../core", version = "2.3.0-alpha.1" }

# Official Rust MCP SDK (Anthropic, modelcontextprotocol/rust-sdk).
# `server` feature enables the request/response handler scaffolding;
# `transport-io` enables the stdio transport. Streamable HTTP comes
# later via the `transport-streamable-http-server` feature.
rmcp = { version = "1.5", default-features = false, features = [
    "server",
    "transport-io",
    "transport-streamable-http-server",
    "macros",
    "schemars",
] }

# Streamable HTTP transport stack — hyper 1.x (matches what rmcp uses
# internally for `transport-streamable-http-server`).
hyper = { version = "1", features = ["server", "http1", "http2"] }
hyper-util = { version = "0.1", features = ["tokio", "server-auto", "service"] }
http = "1"
http-body-util = "0.1"
tower = { version = "0.5", features = ["util"] }
tower-service = "0.3"
bytes = "1"

# Constant-time bearer-token compare. The `subtle` crate is the
# de-facto Rust idiom for timing-safe comparisons.
subtle = "2"

# Per-collection allow-list regex compilation (RBAC, ADR-004 §5).
regex = { version = "1", default-features = false, features = ["std", "perf"] }

# Layered rate limiting per ADR-004 §6 — (transport, principal),
# (principal, backend, collection), (transport).
governor = { version = "0.7", default-features = false, features = ["std", "quanta"] }
dashmap = "6"

# HTTP client for the JWKS fetch loop (--auth jwt with --jwks-url).
# Default features include rustls + json; we don't need the native-TLS path.
reqwest = { version = "0.12", default-features = false, features = ["rustls-tls", "json"] }

# JWT (JWS) validation for `--auth jwt`. ADR-004 §5 SOTA path.
# `use_pem` enables from_rsa_pem / from_ec_pem (RS256/ES256 — v0.5).
# Default features pull rustls-friendly crypto; we don't need the
# OpenSSL backend.
jsonwebtoken = { version = "9", default-features = false, features = ["use_pem"] }

# mTLS — v0.6. tokio-rustls for the TLS handshake; rustls-pemfile
# for loading PEM-encoded server cert + key + client CA bundle.
# rustls is already in the dep tree via reqwest's rustls-tls feature.
tokio-rustls = { version = "0.26", default-features = false, features = ["ring"] }
rustls-pemfile = "2"
rustls-pki-types = "1"
sha2 = "0.10"

# Async runtime used by rmcp's stdio transport.
tokio = { version = "1.39", features = ["rt-multi-thread", "macros", "io-std", "signal", "sync", "net", "time"] }
title: ruvector-rulake-mcp

text:
Rust crate / manifest: ruvector-rulake-ruqu
Path: crates/ruqu-backend/Cargo.toml
Description: ruQu v2 BackendAdapter for ruLake — quantum execution substrate, StateVector + Stabilizer + TensorNetwork backends (ADR-008)

# ruQu backend — quantum execution BackendAdapter (ADR-008).
#
# v0.0 shipped the StateVector backend (small-N exact simulation with
# witness-anchored execution that round-trips through the ruLake
# cache). v0.1 added the Stabilizer backend (Aaronson–Gottesman
# tableau, polynomial-time Clifford-only simulation, qubit cap 32).
# **v0.2 adds the TensorNetwork backend** — a Matrix Product State
# (MPS) simulator using `ndarray` rank-3 tensors with SVD-based
# truncation to a configurable bond-dimension cap. Unlike Stabilizer
# the TensorNetwork backend is universal (handles T / Rz); unlike
# StateVector it scales to 100+ qubits at low entanglement. Clifford+T
# / Hardware backends land in v0.3 per ADR-008 §4.
#
# Standalone Cargo package per ADR-001 (no root workspace; rulake from
# crates.io v2.2 is the only ruLake-side dep).
#
# Scope of v0.2:
#   - `RuquStateVectorBackend` (≤16 qubits, exact f64 amplitudes).
#   - `RuquStabilizerBackend` (≤32 qubits, Clifford-only via tableau).
#   - `RuquTensorNetworkBackend` (≤MAX_QUBITS_TN qubits, MPS with
#     bond-dim cap; supports the full mini-IR including T / Rz).
#   - `Circuit` mini-IR: H, X, Y, Z, S, T, CNOT, RZ. TensorNetwork
#     handles all of these; Stabilizer still refuses T / Rz.
#   - Witness derivation byte-isomorphic to a `RuLakeBundle` —
#     `RuLakeBundle::new(data_ref="ruqu://<circuit-id>@<backend-tag>",
#     dim, rotation_seed, rerank_factor=1, generation)`. The backend
#     tag (`"sv"` / `"stabilizer"` / `"tensor_network"`) flows into
#     the witness; the concordance-mode strip per ADR-008 §G4 is still
#     deferred (now to v0.3).
#
# Build:  cargo build --release
# Test:   cargo test --release
# Bench:  cargo bench --bench tensor_network

[package]
name        = "ruvector-rulake-ruqu"
version     = "0.2.0"
edition     = "2021"
rust-version = "1.89"
license     = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"
authors     = ["Ruvector Team"]
repository  = "https://github.com/ruvnet/RuLake"
description = "ruQu v2 BackendAdapter for ruLake — quantum execution substrate, StateVector + Stabilizer + TensorNetwork backends (ADR-008)"
readme      = "README.md"

[dependencies]
rulake = { path = "../core", version = "2.3.0-alpha.1" }
serde = { version = "1.0", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1.0"
thiserror = "2.0"
sha3 = "0.10"
hex = "0.4"
# v0.2: ndarray rank-3 tensors back the MPS chain. `default-features
# = false` strips the (off-by-default) `serde` and `rayon` features so
# the transitive surface stays flat; we use only the core array API.
ndarray = { version = "0.16", default-features = false }

[dev-dependencies]
tempfile = "3"
criterion = { version = "0.5", features = ["html_reports"] }

[[bench]]
name    = "simulate"
harness = false

[[bench]]
name    = "execute_and_pull"
harness = false

[[bench]]
name    = "stabilizer"
harness = false

[[bench]]
name    = "tensor_network"
harness = false

[profile.release]
opt-level     = 3
lto           = "thin"
codegen-units = 1
title: ruvector-rulake-ruqu

Rust crate / manifest: ruvector-rulake-rvdna
Path: crates/rvdna-backend/Cargo.toml
Description: rvDNA v2 BackendAdapter for ruLake — genomic substrate, T0 hot-tier + T1 warm-mmap tier + T2 cold-lazy tier (ADR-007)

# rvDNA backend — `.rvdna` v2 file-format BackendAdapter (ADR-007).
#
# Hot-tier (T0) implementation for the rvDNA v2 file format: serves
# k-mer vector batches from a memory-mapped `.rvdna` file's section 1
# directly to the ruLake cache. Witness derived from the file's bundle
# pointer at byte 0x00B0 — byte-isomorphic to a `RuLakeBundle` so two
# deployments reading the same `.rvdna` file produce identical SHAKE-256
# witnesses and share cache transparently.
#
# Standalone Cargo package per ADR-001 (no root workspace; rulake from
# crates.io v2.2 is the only ruLake-side dep).
#
# v0.0 ships T0 only. v0.1 adds T1 (warm mmap tier — protein embeddings,
# attention, variant tensors decoded from mmap'd `.rvdna` v2 sections
# §2/§3/§4 — see `src/t1.rs` and `docs/research/rvdna/v2-spec.md`).
# v0.2 adds T2 (cold lazy tier — raw DNA + epigenomic series, sections
# §5–§8). T2 keeps a `std::fs::File` handle (no mmap) and does lazy
# seek+read on each pull, with a small per-collection LRU window so the
# second hit on a range is page-cache fast. See `src/t2.rs`.
#
# Build:  cargo build --release
# Test:   cargo test --release

[package]

license     = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"

[package]

version = "0.1.0"

# Standalone crate. Empty [workspace] keeps cudarc + the CUDA toolchain

[[bin]]
name = "cuda-brute-force"

[dependencies]
# Safe Rust bindings to the CUDA driver / runtime / NVRTC. We use the
# driver API at runtime to load the PTX we compile in build.rs.
# `fallback-dynamic-loading` lets the binary dlopen libcuda at startup
# rather than linking it statically — friendlier on machines without
# libcuda.so on the linker path.
cudarc = { version = "0.19", default-features = false, features = [
    "std",
    "driver",
    "nvrtc",
    "fallback-dynamic-loading",
    # CUDA toolkit version pinned at build time. cudarc requires one of
    # its `cuda-XXXXX` features so it knows which sys-bindings to use.
    # The host has CUDA 13.0; switch to cuda-12080 / 12090 etc. on
    # older toolkits, or use `cuda-version-from-build-system` to let
    # cudarc autodetect by invoking `nvcc --version`.
    "cuda-13000",
] }
sha3 = "0.10"
hex = "0.4"
serde = { version = "1.0", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1.0"

Rust crate / manifest: rulake-py
Path: sdk/python/Cargo.toml
Description: Python bindings for ruLake — vector cache + federation intermediary

# ruLake — Python SDK (PyO3 binding)
#
# Implements ADR-002. Standalone Cargo package — does not declare a
# workspace; cargo discovers the parent rulake crate via the
# `path = ".."` dep, and the vendored ruvector-rabitq via that crate's
# own dep on `vendor/ruvector/...` (ADR-001).
#
# Build:  maturin develop --release
# Test:   cd .. && python -m pytest python/tests
[package]
name = "rulake-py"
version = "2.3.0-alpha.1"
edition = "2021"
license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"
authors = ["Ruvector Team"]
repository = "https://github.com/ruvnet/RuLake"
description = "Python bindings for ruLake — vector cache + federation intermediary"
publish = false

[lib]
# napi-rs / pyo3 both want a `cdylib`. The Python module's import name
# is `_rulake` (see pyproject [tool.maturin].module-name) — the pure-
# Python wrapper at python_src/rulake/__init__.py re-exports from it.
name = "_rulake"
crate-type = ["cdylib"]

[dependencies]
# The cache + router crate one directory up. This is the whole point —
# every `pyo3` wrapper here is a thin shim over the public Rust surface.
rulake = { path = "../../crates/core", version = "2.3.0-alpha.1" }
# PyO3 — abi3-py39 keeps one wheel working across CPython 3.9–3.13.
# The `extension-module` feature is required when building a Python
# extension (otherwise we'd link libpython at build time, breaking
# manylinux wheels).
pyo3 = { version = "0.22", features = ["abi3-py39", "extension-module"] }
# numpy — PyArray + .as_slice()? for zero-copy borrows. Tracks pyo3 0.22.
numpy = "0.22"

[profile.release]
opt-level = 3
lto = "thin"
codegen-units = 1
strip = true

# Quiet PyO3 0.22's `create_exception!` macro hygiene noise. The macro
# internally tests `cfg(gil-refs)` to support both 0.21 (gil-refs default)
# and 0.22 (bound default); rustc 1.80+ flags any cfg name it doesn't see
# in build.rs's `cargo:rustc-check-cfg`. The cfg is real — we just
# don't have it set, which is fine. Drop this when we move to PyO3 0.23+.
[lints.rust]
unexpected_cfgs = { level = "warn", check-cfg = ['cfg(feature, values("gil-refs"))'] }
title: rulake-py

Module examples/gpu/01-cuda-brute-force/build.rs — doc comment:
Compile the CUDA L2 kernel to PTX with `nvcc`.

cudarc loads the resulting PTX at runtime via the driver API, so we
don't need to link against any CUDA libraries at build time. If
`nvcc` is unavailable, the build emits a `cargo:warning` and writes
a stub PTX that the runtime will refuse to load — this keeps
`cargo check` workable on machines without the toolchain while
producing a clear failure at run time.

We deliberately don't `panic!` on a missing `nvcc`: the README is
the authoritative install instruction, and a hard build failure
makes the example uninspectable to readers without the toolchain.

text:
Module examples/gpu/01-cuda-brute-force/src/ruvec1.rs — doc comment:
`ruvec1` binary parser.

Mirrors the on-disk format documented in `src/fs_backend.rs`:

```text
  bytes  field
  0..8   magic         = b"ruvec1\0\0"
  8..16  count : u64   little-endian
 16..20  dim   : u32   little-endian
 20..24  _reserved     (must be zero)
 24..    records × count, each:
           id : u64  little-endian
           v  : f32 × dim  little-endian
```

Bounds checking matches `FsBackend::pull_vectors` — the same
`MAX_PULLED_VECTORS` and `MAX_PULLED_DIM` caps from
`src/backend.rs`. A hostile or corrupt header is rejected before
any allocation happens.

TypeScript types and a hardened parser for the ruLake bundle sidecar
(`table.rulake.json`). Mirrors `src/bundle.rs` in the Rust crate.

The DoS caps are copied verbatim from the Rust implementation so a
malicious bundle cannot force a Node reader to allocate an unbounded
amount of memory:

  - whole bundle JSON  ≤ 64 KiB
  - each string field  ≤  4 KiB
  - rvf_witness        ≤  128 chars (real value is exactly 64 hex)
  - format_version     ≤  2

Serializes as untagged JSON (matches Rust `#[serde(untagged)]`):
  - numeric  → a JSON number that fits in u64
  - opaque   → a JSON string

Bundle ETag policy.

are interchangeable for any query. So we use it directly as the

correct behaviour for a coherence-anchored sidecar — bundles are tiny

Module examples/nodejs/02-bundle-publisher/src/watcher.ts — doc comment:
Filesystem watcher for ruLake publish directories.

The Rust `publish_bundle(key, dir)` writes

    <root>/<backend>/<collection>/table.rulake.json

Brute-force exact L2 nearest-K over the items extracted from a ruLake
snapshot.

reads HTTP responses from a Rust ruLake see the same thing.

ruLake search backend; this is the agentic substrate, not the
production serving path.

Module examples/nodejs/04-mcp-tool/src/snapshot.ts — doc comment:
Load and verify a ruLake snapshot directory.

A snapshot, written by the Rust crate's `RuLake::save_cache_to_dir`,
contains:

  <dir>/table.rulake.json   # the bundle sidecar (ADR-155)
  <dir>/index.rbpx           # rabitq-persist payload (header + items)

The `.rbpx` format is documented in
`vendor/ruvector/crates/ruvector-rabitq/src/persist.rs`:

  | offset | size              | field                       |
  |--------|-------------------|-----------------------------|
  |   0    |  8                | magic = b"rbpx0001"         |
  |   8    |  4                | version (u32 LE, currently 1)|
  |  12    |  4                | dim (u32 LE)                |
  |  16    |  8                | seed (u64 LE)               |
  |  24    |  4                | rerank_factor (u32 LE)      |
  |  28    |  4                | n (u32 LE)                  |
  |  32    |  n × (4 + dim·4) | id (u32 LE) + dim·f32 LE    |

Bounds (matched here so we behave identically to the Rust loader):
  dim        ≤ 8192
  n          ≤ 100_000_000
  rerank     ≤ 1024

The Node side does NOT have the RaBitQ decompressor, so this loader
exposes the *original* (id, vector) pairs that the Rust loader uses
to deterministically rebuild the index. Brute-force L2 over those
title: snapshot.ts

Module examples/sidecar_daemon.rs — doc comment:
Minimal cache-sidecar daemon demonstrating the bundle protocol
(ADR-155 §Consequences).

Watches a publish directory for updates to `table.rulake.json`
and calls `RuLake::refresh_from_bundle_dir` to keep the reader
cache coherent with whatever the publisher has signed off.

Run with:
  cargo run --release -p rulake --example sidecar_daemon

The example simulates a full deployment in one process:
  - A "publisher" backend with a collection of vectors
  - A "reader" RuLake serving queries against the same collection
  - The publisher updates the backend and emits a new bundle
  - The reader's daemon polls, detects the witness change,
    invalidates, and the next query re-primes automatically

A real deployment replaces the polling loop with an inotify
watcher or GCS object-change notification; the shape is identical.
title: sidecar_daemon.rs

text:
Module examples/warm_restart.rs — doc comment:
Save -> ship -> warm-restart end-to-end demo for ruLake.

Shows the three operator phases a real warm-handoff goes through:

  1. PUBLISHER: prime a RuLake cache from a backend, snapshot the
     compressed index + witnessed bundle sidecar to a directory.
  2. READER:    a brand-new RuLake process (no backend registered)
     calls `warm_from_dir` on that same directory and is serving
     queries in milliseconds, bypassing the backend round-trip and
     RaBitQ compression entirely.
  3. COLD:      for comparison, another fresh RuLake with the
     backend registered but no warm snapshot pays the full
     prime-from-backend cost on its first query.

The summary at the end reports the speedup of warm-from-disk vs.
cold-prime-from-backend plus steady-state QPS for both — the QPS
should be nearly identical because they end up with the same
compressed index; only the first-query cost differs.

Run with:
  cargo run -p rulake --release --example warm_restart

text:
Module ui/src/lib/embed.js — doc comment:
Embedding provider — turns the Playground's query text into a vector.

Providers wired here:
  none      — deterministic mulberry32 fake (default; no network).
  openai    — text-embedding-3-small via /v1/embeddings (1536-d).
  cohere    — embed-english-v3 via /v1/embed (1024-d).
  voyage    — voyage-3-lite via /v1/embeddings (512-d).
  webllm    — local Web-LLM via WebGPU (not wired this iteration).

API keys live in JS memory only. The provider/key choice is exposed
at runtime via `window.RULakeEmbed.configure({...})` — populated by
the Storage settings card on the Connect screen.
title: embed.js

text:
Module ui/src/lib/http.js — doc comment:
rulake/http — HTTP client variant (v2 surface, ADR-003 §"What's not yet here").

Lightweight fetch-based client for talking to a remote `rulake-mcp`
server (the Streamable HTTP transport added in mcp-server v0.2). Lets
edge runtimes that can't load the native binary — Cloudflare Workers,
Deno-deploy, browser ServiceWorkers — still consume a remote ruLake
memory layer through one MCP tool.

Pairs with `rulake-wasm` for the local witness-verification side: any
hit returned by the remote can be re-verified locally against its
bundle witness with `rulake-wasm`'s `verifyBundleJson`.
Cheap deterministic-ish nonce per request — the server's replay
guard rejects duplicates.
title: http.js

text:
Module ui/src/lib/searchOffload.js — doc comment:
Search dispatcher — picks worker or main-thread path based on the
user's Workers toggle in the Storage settings card.

The worker is created lazily on first use; subsequent calls reuse it.
Each call gets a fresh request-id so concurrent requests don't
collide.

Run an exact-L2 nearest-K search.
title: searchOffload.js

text:
Module ui/src/lib/wasm.js — doc comment:
Lazy-loader for the rulake-wasm package (~149 KB compressed).
Exposed on window.RULakeWasm so the JSX files (which use globals) can
call it. Loaded on demand — first call triggers the dynamic import.

The wasm-bindgen module exports:
  verifyBundleJson(json) → {ok, computed, stored, fields}
  computeWitness(data_ref, dim, rotation_seed, rerank_factor, generation)
  searchBruteForceL2(vectors, ids, dim, query, k) → [{idx, id, score}]
  formatVersion() → 2
  buildInfo() → "rulake-wasm v2.2.0 (witness-format v2, sha3 = 0.10)"
The 'bundler' target export needs no init() (Vite handles it).
Some targets export init as default — try it if present, ignore failures.
title: wasm.js

text:
Module ui/src/main.jsx — doc comment:
ruLake Console — Vite entry.

The design ships as plain-JS / babel-standalone files that each
declare functions at top level and `Object.assign(window, {...})` at
the bottom. Their first lines do `const { useState } = React;`, which
expects React to already be a global. ESM hoists static imports above
any top-level statements, so we use *dynamic* imports below to delay
side-effect loading until AFTER React/ReactDOM have been pinned on
`window`.
Styles first so first paint isn't unstyled.
Load the design files in the same order ruLake Console.html does.
Each file's body runs synchronously and writes its exports onto
`window` — later imports can read them.
wasm side-loader — populates window.RULakeWasm with lazy-load
shims for verifyBundle / computeWitness / searchL2. The rulake-wasm
chunk (~149 KB) only fetches when one of those is first called.
title: main.jsx

text:
Module ui/src/workers/search.worker.js — doc comment:
Web Worker — exact L2 nearest-K, off the main thread.

Mirrors `rulake-wasm::searchBruteForceL2` semantics (recall = 1.0,
k capped at min(n, 4096)) but runs in pure JS so the worker boots
without needing wasm in worker-scope (Vite + wasm-bindgen require
extra plumbing for that — a v0.2 polish). The win we ship today is
"the search runs off the main thread" — which is what the Workers
toggle in the Storage settings card is advertising.

Protocol:
  inbound: { id, type: 'search', vectors: Float32Array, ids: Float64Array,
             dim, query: Float32Array, k }
  outbound: { id, type: 'result', hits: [{idx, id, score}], ms }
  on error: { id, type: 'error', message }
title: search.worker.js

# Continuous integration — every push and PR.
#
# Builds and tests every shipped crate so a green main is "everything
# works on Linux x86_64". Per-platform release builds live in the
# release-* workflows.

name: ci

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  RUST_BACKTRACE: 1

jobs:
  rust:
    name: Rust — ${{ matrix.crate }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        # Every sibling Cargo package per ADR-001 (no root workspace).
        # Storage adapters, substrate adapters, and MCP companion
        # servers all build + test independently.
        crate:
          - "crates/core"
          - "crates/mcp-server"
          - "crates/mcp-rvdna"
          - "crates/mcp-ruqu"
          - "crates/gcs-backend"
          - "crates/ipfs-backend"
          - "crates/rvdna-backend"
          - "crates/ruqu-backend"
          - "crates/kernel-avx512"   # ADR-157 SIMD reference impl (issue #3)
          - "crates/kernel-wgpu"     # ADR-157 portable GPU impl (issue #3)
          - "sdk/python"
          - "sdk/node"
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          submodules: recursive   # ADR-001 requires vendor/ruvector
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: ${{ matrix.crate }}
      - name: Build
        working-directory: ${{ matrix.crate }}
        run: cargo build --release
      - name: Test
        # The sdk/python + sdk/node crates have no Rust-side tests of
        # their own (their tests run in pytest / node --test). Skip in
        # those rows; the release-python / release-node workflows cover them.
        if: matrix.crate != 'sdk/python' && matrix.crate != 'sdk/node'
        working-directory: ${{ matrix.crate }}
        run: cargo test --release

  python-tests:
    name: Python SDK — pytest
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          submodules: recursive
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - name: Build + test
        # `maturin develop` requires an active virtualenv (or CONDA_PREFIX,
        # or a `.venv` it can find). The hosted runner's system Python
        # has neither, so we create a `.venv` per job, install build +
        # test deps into it, and let maturin install the wheel into it.
        working-directory: sdk/python
        run: |
          python -m venv .venv
          source .venv/bin/activate
          pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install maturin pytest numpy
          maturin develop --release
          pytest tests/ -v

  node-tests:
    name: Node SDK — node --test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          submodules: recursive
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "22"
      - name: Build native binding
        working-directory: sdk/node
        run: |
          cargo build --release
          # The crate is named `rulake-node` (sdk/node/Cargo.toml:1), so
          # cargo emits `librulake_node.so` — not the older
          # `libruvector_rulake_node.so` name from before the rename.
          cp target/release/librulake_node.so rulake.linux-x64-gnu.node
      - name: Run smoke tests
        working-directory: sdk/node
        run: node --test __test__/smoke.test.mjs
title: ci.yml

text:
--release
          # The crate is named `rulake-node` (sdk/node/Cargo.toml:1), so
          # cargo emits `librulake_node.so` — not the older
          # `libruvector_rulake_node.so` name from before the rename.
          cp target/release/librulake_node.so rulake.linux-x64-gnu.node
      - name: Run smoke tests
        working-directory: sdk/node
        run: node --test __test__/smoke.test.mjs

  smoke:
    # End-to-end smoke per the README's smoke contracts table:
    # WASM-local Console, mcp-rvdna HTTP, and Console + mcp-rvdna
    # cross-component. Catches regressions a single-crate cargo test
    # would miss (e.g. iter 32's CORS + SSE-parser bugs).
    name: Smoke — scripts/smoke-all.sh
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: rust   # only run when every crate built green
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          submodules: recursive
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "22"
      - uses: browser-actions/setup-chrome@v1
      - name: Pre-install agent-browser (warms npx cache)
        run: npx --yes agent-browser install || true
      - name: Build mcp-server binary (enables smoke-all auto --live)
        working-directory: crates/mcp-server
        run: cargo build --release --bin rulake-mcp
      - name: Build mcp-rvdna binary
        working-directory: crates/mcp-rvdna
        run: cargo build --release --bin rvdna-mcp
      - name: "Install + build sdk/node-wasm (rulake-wasm sibling, file: dep)"
        # ui depends on rulake-wasm via `file:../sdk/node-wasm`. Vite picks
        # the package.json `exports.".".browser` entry which is `./web/...`,
        # but `web/` and `nodejs/` are gitignored (wasm-pack outputs).
        # Build them now or Vite hard-fails with
        # `[commonjs--resolver] Failed to resolve entry for package "rulake-wasm"`.
        # Mirror what release-ui.yml does.
        run: |
          rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown
          cargo install --locked wasm-pack || true
          (cd sdk/node-wasm && unset RUSTFLAGS CARGO_BUILD_RUSTFLAGS && ./build.sh)
      - name: Install ui deps + build dist
        working-directory: ui
        run: |
          npm ci || npm install
          npm run build
      - name: Run all three smokes via scripts/smoke-all.sh
        run: ./scripts/smoke-all.sh
title: ci.yml

Config .github/workflows/release-docker.yml:
# Release the rulake-mcp Docker image to GHCR.
#
# Triggered manually or on tag `mcp-v*`. Builds the distroless image
# defined by deploy/Dockerfile.mcp and pushes:
#   ghcr.io/ruvnet/rulake-mcp:<tag>     (e.g. mcp-v0.3.0)
#   ghcr.io/ruvnet/rulake-mcp:latest    (on tag push, not workflow_dispatch)
#
# Uses the GITHUB_TOKEN's packages:write scope — no extra secrets needed.

name: release-docker

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - "mcp-v*"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tag:
        description: "Image tag (default: dev)"
        type: string
        default: dev

env:
  REGISTRY: ghcr.io
  IMAGE_NAME: ${{ github.repository_owner }}/rulake-mcp

jobs:
  build-and-push:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          submodules: recursive
      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
      - name: Log in to GHCR
        uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          registry: ${{ env.REGISTRY }}
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      - name: Compute tags
        id: meta
        uses: docker/metadata-action@v5
        with:
          images: ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}
          tags: |
            type=raw,value=${{ github.event.inputs.tag || 'latest' }},enable=${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/mcp-v') }}
            type=match,pattern=mcp-v(.*),group=1
            type=sha,prefix=sha-
      - name: Build + push
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
        with:
          context: .
          file: deploy/Dockerfile.mcp
          push: true
          tags: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tags }}
          labels: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.labels }}
          cache-from: type=gha
          cache-to: type=gha,mode=max
title: release-docker.yml

Config .github/workflows/release-mcp-bin.yml:
# Release rulake-mcp prebuilt binaries to GitHub Releases.
#
# Triggered manually or on tag `mcp-v*`. Builds rulake-mcp for the
# five core platforms (matches the SDKs' coverage) and uploads each
# as a tarball/zip to the GitHub Release for the tag.

name: release-mcp-bin

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - "mcp-v*"
  workflow_dispatch:

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  PACKAGE_DIR: crates/mcp-server
  BIN: rulake-mcp

jobs:
  build:
    name: build (${{ matrix.target.triple }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.target.os }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        target:
          - { os: ubuntu-latest,   triple: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu,  archive: tar.gz }
          - { os: ubuntu-latest,   triple: aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, archive: tar.gz, cross: true }
          - { os: macos-13,        triple: x86_64-apple-darwin,        archive: tar.gz }
          - { os: macos-14,        triple: aarch64-apple-darwin,       archive: tar.gz }
          - { os: windows-latest,  triple: x86_64-pc-windows-msvc,     archive: zip }
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          submodules: recursive
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          targets: ${{ matrix.target.triple }}
      - name: Cross-compile shim (linux-aarch64)
        if: matrix.target.cross == true
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y gcc-aarch64-linux-gnu
          echo 'CARGO_TARGET_AARCH64_UNKNOWN_LINUX_GNU_LINKER=aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc' >> $GITHUB_ENV
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: ${{ env.PACKAGE_DIR }}
      - name: Build
        working-directory: ${{ env.PACKAGE_DIR }}
        run: cargo build --release --target ${{ matrix.target.triple }} --bin ${{ env.BIN }}
      - name: Stage artifact (unix)
        if: matrix.target.archive == 'tar.gz'
        working-directory: ${{ env.PACKAGE_DIR }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          mkdir -p staging
          cp target/${{ matrix.target.triple }}/release/${{ env.BIN }} staging/
          cp ../../README.md ../../LICENSE-* staging/ 2>/dev/null || true
          tar -czf ${{ env.BIN }}-${{ matrix.target.triple }}.tar.gz -C staging .
      - name: Stage artifact (windows)
        if: matrix.target.archive == 'zip'
        working-directory: ${{ env.PACKAGE_DIR }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          mkdir -p staging
          cp target/${{ matrix.target.triple }}/release/${{ env.BIN }}.exe staging/
          cp ../../README.md staging/ 2>/dev/null || true
          7z a ${{ env.BIN }}-${{ matrix.target.triple }}.zip ./staging/*
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: bin-${{ matrix.target.triple }}
          path: |
            ${{ env.PACKAGE_DIR }}/${{ env.BIN }}-${{ matrix.target.triple }}.tar.gz
            ${{ env.PACKAGE_DIR }}/${{ env.BIN }}-${{ matrix.target.triple }}.zip

  release:
    name: attach to GitHub Release
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/mcp-v')
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          path: dist
          merge-multiple: true
      - uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v2
        with:
          files: |
            dist/*.tar.gz
            dist/*.zip
          generate_release_notes: true
title: release-mcp-bin.yml

text:
Config .github/workflows/release-node.yml:
# Release Node SDK — per-platform .node binaries via napi-rs (ADR-003 §5).
#
# Triggered manually (workflow_dispatch) or on a tag matching
# `node-v*` (e.g. node-v2.2.0). Builds five platform binaries and
# publishes one umbrella package + five `optionalDependencies`
# packages on npm — the Prisma / next-swc pattern.
#
# Publishes when NPM_TOKEN is set in repo secrets.

name: release-node

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - "node-v*"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      publish:
        description: "Publish to npm"
        type: boolean
        default: false

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  PACKAGE_DIR: sdk/node

jobs:
  build:
    name: build (${{ matrix.target.triple }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.target.os }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        target:
          - { os: ubuntu-latest,   triple: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu,  artifact: rulake.linux-x64-gnu.node }
          - { os: ubuntu-latest,   triple: aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, artifact: rulake.linux-arm64-gnu.node }
          - { os: macos-13,        triple: x86_64-apple-darwin,        artifact: rulake.darwin-x64.node }
          - { os: macos-14,        triple: aarch64-apple-darwin,       artifact: rulake.darwin-arm64.node }
          - { os: windows-latest,  triple: x86_64-pc-windows-msvc,     artifact: rulake.win32-x64-msvc.node }
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          submodules: recursive
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          targets: ${{ matrix.target.triple }}
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "22"
      - name: Cross-compile shim (linux-aarch64 only)
        if: matrix.target.triple == 'aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y gcc-aarch64-linux-gnu
          echo 'CARGO_TARGET_AARCH64_UNKNOWN_LINUX_GNU_LINKER=aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc' >> $GITHUB_ENV
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: ${{ env.PACKAGE_DIR }}
      - name: Install @napi-rs/cli
        working-directory: ${{ env.PACKAGE_DIR }}
        run: npm install --no-save @napi-rs/cli@^2.18.4
      - name: Build .node binary
        working-directory: ${{ env.PACKAGE_DIR }}
        run: npx napi build --platform --release --target ${{ matrix.target.triple }}
      - name: Stage artifact
        working-directory: ${{ env.PACKAGE_DIR }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          # napi build emits the binary in the package root with the
          # right filename based on --target; rename if needed.
          if [ ! -f "${{ matrix.target.artifact }}" ]; then
            ls -la *.node 2>/dev/null || true
            echo "expected ${{ matrix.target.artifact }} not produced; falling back to first .node"
            mv $(ls *.node | head -1) ${{ matrix.target.artifact }}
          fi
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: node-binary-${{ matrix.target.triple }}
          path: ${{ env.PACKAGE_DIR }}/${{ matrix.target.artifact }}

        with:
          name: node-binary-${{ matrix.target.triple }}
          path: ${{ env.PACKAGE_DIR }}/${{ matrix.target.artifact }}

  publish:
    name: publish to npm
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: |
      startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/node-v') ||
      (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.event.inputs.publish == 'true')
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          submodules: recursive
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          registry-url: "https://registry.npmjs.org"
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          path: ${{ env.PACKAGE_DIR }}/artifacts
      - name: Stage binaries into the umbrella package
        working-directory: ${{ env.PACKAGE_DIR }}
        run: |
          shopt -s globstar
          for f in artifacts/**/*.node; do
            cp "$f" .
          done
          ls -la *.node
      - name: Publish per-platform packages + umbrella
        working-directory: ${{ env.PACKAGE_DIR }}
        env:
          NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          # @napi-rs/cli's `napi prepublish --skip-gh-release` walks
          # the napi.triples in package.json, builds per-platform
          # sub-packages (@ruvector/rulake-<triple>) and publishes
          # them, then publishes the umbrella package with the right
          # optionalDependencies. The Prisma / next-swc pattern.
          npm install --no-save @napi-rs/cli@^2.18.4
          npx napi prepublish --tag latest --skip-gh-release
          npm publish --access public

text:
Config .github/workflows/release-python.yml:
# Release Python SDK — ABI3 wheels per ADR-002 §5.
#
# Triggered manually (workflow_dispatch) or on a tag matching
# `python-v*` (e.g. python-v2.2.0). Builds five wheels:
# - manylinux_2_28 x86_64
# - manylinux_2_28 aarch64
# - macOS x86_64 (Intel)
# - macOS aarch64 (Apple Silicon)
# - Windows x86_64
# - sdist (always)
#
# Publishes to PyPI when PYPI_API_TOKEN is set in repo secrets.

name: release-python

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - "python-v*"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      publish:
        description: "Publish to PyPI"
        type: boolean
        default: false

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  PACKAGE_DIR: sdk/python

jobs:
  build:
    name: build (${{ matrix.platform.target }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.platform.os }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        platform:
          - { os: ubuntu-latest,    target: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu,  manylinux: 2_28, name: linux-x86_64 }
          - { os: ubuntu-latest,    target: aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, manylinux: 2_28, name: linux-aarch64 }
          - { os: macos-13,         target: x86_64-apple-darwin,                       name: macos-x86_64 }
          - { os: macos-14,         target: aarch64-apple-darwin,                      name: macos-aarch64 }
          - { os: windows-latest,   target: x86_64-pc-windows-msvc,                    name: windows-x86_64 }
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          submodules: recursive
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - name: Build wheel via maturin-action
        uses: PyO3/maturin-action@v1
        with:
          working-directory: ${{ env.PACKAGE_DIR }}
          target: ${{ matrix.platform.target }}
          manylinux: ${{ matrix.platform.manylinux || 'auto' }}
          args: --release --out dist
          # ADR-002 requires ABI3-py39: one wheel per platform per release.
          # `extension-module` is set in pyproject.toml.
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: wheel-${{ matrix.platform.name }}
          path: ${{ env.PACKAGE_DIR }}/dist/*.whl

  sdist:
    name: build sdist
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          submodules: recursive    # critical — pyproject.toml [tool.maturin].include pulls vendored sources
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - name: Build sdist
        uses: PyO3/maturin-action@v1
        with:
          working-directory: ${{ env.PACKAGE_DIR }}
          command: sdist
          args: --out dist
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: sdist
          path: ${{ env.PACKAGE_DIR }}/dist/*.tar.gz

  publish:
    name: publish to PyPI
    needs: [build, sdist]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Only publish on tag push or explicit workflow_dispatch with publish=true.
    if: |
      startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/python-v') ||
      (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.event.inputs.publish == 'true')
    environment:
      name: pypi
      url: https://pypi.org/p/ruvector-rulake
    permissions:
      id-token: write       # OIDC trusted publishing (preferred over PYPI_API_TOKEN)
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          path: dist
          merge-multiple: true
      - uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1
        with:
          packages-dir: dist
          # Falls back to PYPI_API_TOKEN secret if OIDC isn't configured.
          # password: ${{ secrets.PYPI_API_TOKEN }}
title: release-python.yml

text:
Config .github/workflows/release-rust.yml:
# Release the Rust crate `ruvector-rulake` to crates.io.
#
# Triggered manually or on tag `rust-v*`. Per ADR-001, the parent
# crate depends on `vendor/ruvector/crates/ruvector-rabitq` via a
# git-submodule path-dep. crates.io publish requires that the path
# dep be embedded in the published .crate (cargo handles this with
# `cargo package --no-verify` since the submodule is on disk after
# `actions/checkout` recursive).
#
# Gated on CRATES_IO_TOKEN secret. Dry-run by default — no-op
# unless explicitly opted in.

name: release-rust

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - "rust-v*"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      publish:
        description: "Publish to crates.io (uncheck for dry-run)"
        type: boolean
        default: false

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always

jobs:
  publish:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          submodules: recursive   # vendor/ruvector must be present
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
      - name: Build + test
        working-directory: crates/core
        run: |
          cargo build --release
          cargo test --release
      - name: Package (sanity check; doesn't publish)
        working-directory: crates/core
        run: cargo package --allow-dirty --no-verify
      - name: Publish to crates.io
        if: |
          startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/rust-v') ||
          (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.event.inputs.publish == 'true')
        working-directory: crates/core
        env:
          CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CRATES_IO_TOKEN }}
        run: cargo publish --allow-dirty --no-verify
title: release-rust.yml

text:
Config .github/workflows/release-ui.yml:
# ruLake Console — Vite + React static SPA, deployed to GitHub Pages.
# Per ADR-006 (docs/adrs/ADR-006-rulake-console-vite-github-pages.md).
# Re-registered after the iter 50 merge to refresh GitHub's workflow
# cache so workflow_dispatch becomes invokable on main.
#
# Triggers:
#   - push to main with paths ui/** (rolling demo at the Pages URL)
#   - push of tags ui-v*  (cut releases — same build, kept for tracking)
#   - workflow_dispatch (manual)
#
# No gh-pages branch — uses the official actions/deploy-pages@v4 OIDC flow.

name: release-ui

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - "ui/**"
      - "sdk/node-wasm/**"
      - ".github/workflows/release-ui.yml"
    tags:
      - "ui-v*"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

concurrency:
  group: "pages"
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build:
    name: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          submodules: recursive

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "22"

      - name: "Install + build sdk/node-wasm (rulake-wasm sibling, file: dep)"
        run: |
          # ui/ depends on rulake-wasm via `file:../sdk/node-wasm`. wasm-pack
          # build emits the artifacts the package.json files[] field
          # publishes. Skip wasm-opt (host wasm-pack's bundled binary
          # rejects rustc bulk-memory ops; we build raw and Vite serves
          # them as-is).
          rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown
          cargo install --locked wasm-pack || true
          (cd sdk/node-wasm && unset RUSTFLAGS CARGO_BUILD_RUSTFLAGS && ./build.sh)

      - name: Install ui/ deps
        working-directory: ui
        run: npm ci || npm install

      - name: Build static SPA
        working-directory: ui
        env:
          VITE_BASE: /RuLake/
        run: npm run build

      # Smoke test gate — runs the same scripts/smoke.sh that local
      # /loop iterations use. Failures show up in the CI log with the
      # exact missing audit code or browser console error. Non-fatal
      # for now (continue-on-error: true) until the runner image's
      # Chrome install is verified across runs; flip to fatal once
      # a green CI run lands.
      - name: E2E smoke (build + preview + agent-browser)
        working-directory: ui
        continue-on-error: true
        run: |
          # Use the SPA's gh-pages base for the smoke too.
          export VITE_BASE=/RuLake/
          npx --yes agent-browser install --with-deps || \
            npx --yes agent-browser install || true
          ./scripts/smoke.sh

      - name: Upload Pages artifact
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
        with:
          path: ui/dist

  deploy:
    name: deploy
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4
title: release-ui.yml

text:
Config .github/workflows/uptime.yml:
# Live-MCP uptime probes — closes issue #8.
#
# Hits each of the three production MCP endpoints every 15 min using
# scripts/smoke-live.sh (the same script `scripts/smoke-all.sh` uses for
# its production rows), then writes a shields.io endpoint-format JSON
# per target into badges/. The README references those JSON files via
# https://img.shields.io/endpoint?url=... so the README's status badges
# flip red within ~15 min of any target going down.
#
# Why 15 min, not 5: Cloud Run scales to zero. Hitting it more
# aggressively would just measure cold-start latency and produce false
# RED on healthy services. 15 min matches the README's CTA expectation
# ("the wire's up") without paying for warm instances.
#
# Why we commit to main (not gh-pages): the JSON files are <100 B each,
# rebuilt every 15 min, and shields.io reads them via raw.githubusercontent
# off main — no Pages build needed. The commit message + [skip ci] tag
# keeps these out of the ci.yml + release-* workflows' notification
# stream.

name: uptime

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/15 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch: {}

permissions:
  contents: write       # required to push badges/*.json back to main
  issues: write         # required for the optional auto-issue on first failure

jobs:
  probe:
    name: Probe live MCPs + refresh badges
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # Probe each target independently. We capture the per-target
      # exit code (smoke-live.sh exits 1 on any assertion failure) and
      # synthesize the shields.io JSON from it. We deliberately do NOT
      # `set -e` the whole step so one red probe doesn't skip the others
      # — the badge for a healthy sibling should still flip green.
      - name: Probe rulake-mcp.ruv.io (8 tools)
        id: rulake
        continue-on-error: true
        run: |
          set +e
          URL=https://rulake-mcp.ruv.io/ EXPECTED_TOOLS=8 ./scripts/smoke-live.sh
          echo "exit_code=$?" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Probe rvdna-mcp.ruv.io (5 tools)
        id: rvdna
        continue-on-error: true
        run: |
          set +e
          URL=https://rvdna-mcp.ruv.io/ EXPECTED_TOOLS=5 ./scripts/smoke-live.sh
          echo "exit_code=$?" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Probe ruqu-mcp.ruv.io (5 tools)
        id: ruqu
        continue-on-error: true
        run: |
          set +e
          URL=https://ruqu-mcp.ruv.io/ EXPECTED_TOOLS=5 ./scripts/smoke-live.sh
          echo "exit_code=$?" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Generate shields.io endpoint JSON for each target
        run: |
          mkdir -p badges
          gen_badge() {
            local label="$1"
            local tools="$2"
            local exit_code="$3"
            local file="badges/${label}.json"
            if [ "${exit_code}" = "0" ]; then
              printf '{"schemaVersion":1,"label":"%s","message":"up · %s tools","color":"brightgreen"}\n' \
                "${label}" "${tools}" > "${file}"
            else
              printf '{"schemaVersion":1,"label":"%s","message":"down","color":"red"}\n' \
                "${label}" > "${file}"
            fi
            echo "wrote ${file}: $(cat ${file})"
          }
          gen_badge "rulake-mcp" 8 "${{ steps.rulake.outputs.exit_code }}"
          gen_badge "rvdna-mcp"  5 "${{ steps.rvdna.outputs.exit_code }}"
          gen_badge "ruqu-mcp"   5 "${{ steps.ruqu.outputs.exit_code }}"
title: uptime.yml

text:
emaVersion":1,"label":"%s","message":"down","color":"red"}\n' \
                "${label}" > "${file}"
            fi
            echo "wrote ${file}: $(cat ${file})"
          }
          gen_badge "rulake-mcp" 8 "${{ steps.rulake.outputs.exit_code }}"
          gen_badge "rvdna-mcp"  5 "${{ steps.rvdna.outputs.exit_code }}"
          gen_badge "ruqu-mcp"   5 "${{ steps.ruqu.outputs.exit_code }}"

      # Commit only if a badge actually changed. Empty `git diff --cached`
      # → skip the commit so we don't spam main with "no-op uptime probe"
      # commits when every target is steady-state green.
      - name: Commit refreshed badges to main
        run: |
          git config user.name  "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git add badges/
          if git diff --cached --quiet; then
            echo "no badge changes — skipping commit"
            exit 0
          fi
          git commit -m "ci(uptime): refresh live-MCP status badges [skip ci]"
          # Push to whatever branch the workflow is running on (main on
          # schedule, the dispatching branch on workflow_dispatch).
          git push origin "HEAD:${GITHUB_REF#refs/heads/}"

      # Optional auto-issue on red. Only opens one issue per outage —
      # checks for an existing open issue with the `live-down` label
      # before filing a new one. Skip with comment if you don't want
      # this; the badge alone is enough signal for most operators.
      - name: Open `live-down` issue on first red
        if: |
          steps.rulake.outputs.exit_code != '0' ||
          steps.rvdna.outputs.exit_code  != '0' ||
          steps.ruqu.outputs.exit_code   != '0'
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            const failed = [];
            if ('${{ steps.rulake.outputs.exit_code }}' !== '0') failed.push('rulake-mcp.ruv.io');
            if ('${{ steps.rvdna.outputs.exit_code  }}' !== '0') failed.push('rvdna-mcp.ruv.io');
            if ('${{ steps.ruqu.outputs.exit_code   }}' !== '0') failed.push('ruqu-mcp.ruv.io');

            const { data: existing } = await github.rest.issues.listForRepo({
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo:  context.repo.repo,
              state: 'open',
              labels: 'live-down',
            });
            if (existing.length > 0) {
              core.info(`live-down issue #${existing[0].number} already open — not filing duplicate`);
              return;
            }

            await github.rest.issues.create({
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo:  context.repo.repo,
              title: `live-MCP down: ${failed.join(', ')}`,
              labels: ['live-down'],
              body: [
                `Uptime workflow detected RED on the following live MCP target(s):`,
                ``,
                ...failed.map(t => `- \`${t}\``),
                ``,
                `Workflow run: ${context.serverUrl}/${context.repo.owner}/${context.repo.repo}/actions/runs/${context.runId}`,
                ``,
                `Auto-filed by \`.github/workflows/uptime.yml\`. Will not refile while open.`,
              ].join('\n'),
            });
title: uptime.yml

text:
Config .github/workflows/validate-marketplace.yml:
# Validates the ruLake plugin marketplace catalog on every push + PR.
#
# Catches the failure modes the ADR-009 marketplace.json contract is
# vulnerable to:
#   1. JSON parse error
#   2. A `source:` path in marketplace.json that doesn't exist in the repo
#   3. A plugin without a `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`
#   4. A plugin.json missing `name` / `version` / `description`
#   5. Plugin `name` field disagreeing with the marketplace.json entry
#
# Note: cross-checking plugin version against parent crate version is
# deferred until the version-bump helper script lands (ADR-009 §C).

name: validate-marketplace

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - ".claude-plugin/**"
      - "plugins/**"
      - ".github/workflows/validate-marketplace.yml"
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - ".claude-plugin/**"
      - "plugins/**"
      - ".github/workflows/validate-marketplace.yml"

jobs:
  validate:
    name: validate marketplace.json
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Marketplace JSON parses
        run: |
          jq empty .claude-plugin/marketplace.json
          echo "✓ marketplace.json parses"

      - name: Every source path exists
        run: |
          fail=0
          jq -r '.plugins[].source' .claude-plugin/marketplace.json | while read src; do
            if [[ ! -d "${src}" ]]; then
              echo "✗ source path missing: ${src}"
              fail=1
            fi
          done
          test "${fail}" -eq 0 || exit 1
          echo "✓ all source paths exist"

      - name: Every plugin has plugin.json with required fields
        run: |
          fail=0
          for d in plugins/*/; do
            mf="${d}.claude-plugin/plugin.json"
            if [[ ! -f "${mf}" ]]; then
              echo "✗ missing manifest: ${mf}"
              fail=1
              continue
            fi
            jq empty "${mf}" || { echo "✗ ${mf} does not parse"; fail=1; continue; }
            for field in name version description; do
              if ! jq -e ".${field}" "${mf}" >/dev/null; then
                echo "✗ ${mf} missing required field: ${field}"
                fail=1
              fi
            done
          done
          test "${fail}" -eq 0 || exit 1
          echo "✓ every plugin manifest is well-formed"

      - name: Plugin name in manifest matches marketplace entry
        run: |
          fail=0
          jq -r '.plugins[] | "\(.name) \(.source)"' .claude-plugin/marketplace.json | while read name src; do
            mf="${src}/.claude-plugin/plugin.json"
            mname=$(jq -r '.name' "${mf}")
            if [[ "${name}" != "${mname}" ]]; then
              echo "✗ marketplace name '${name}' != plugin.json name '${mname}' for ${src}"
              fail=1
            fi
          done
          test "${fail}" -eq 0 || exit 1
          echo "✓ marketplace + plugin.json names agree"

      - name: .mcp.json files parse where present
        run: |
          fail=0
          for f in plugins/*/.mcp.json; do
            test -f "${f}" || continue
            jq empty "${f}" || { echo "✗ ${f} does not parse"; fail=1; }
          done
          test "${fail}" -eq 0 || exit 1
          echo "✓ all .mcp.json files parse"
title: validate-marketplace.yml

Config crates/mcp-server/tests/fixtures/mcp.toml:
# Sample mcp.toml for the v0.1 server.
#
# Drop more backends here. v0.1 supports `local` (in-memory; the
# operator pre-populates collections in code) and `fs` (filesystem-
# backed `ruvec1` files). Real cloud backends (Parquet, BigQuery,
# Iceberg, Delta) land per ADR-155 §M2-M5.

consistency  = { mode = "Eventual", ttl_ms = 5000 }
rerank_factor = 20
rotation_seed = 42
workers       = 0    # 0 = cores * 2 (ADR-004 §6 default)
max_inflight  = 64

[[backends]]
type = "local"
id   = "demo"

# An fs-backend example with one pre-registered collection. The file
# itself isn't created here — operators load it via FsBackend::write
# in their own code (or via the existing rulake-demo binary).
#
# [[backends]]
# type = "fs"
# id   = "lake-prod"
# root = "/srv/rulake/lake-prod"
#
# [[backends.collections]]
# name     = "memories"
# filename = "memories.ruvec1"
title: mcp.toml

Config examples/python/01-verify-witness/pyproject.toml:
[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=68", "wheel"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[project]
name = "rulake-verify-witness"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "Pure-Python verifier for ruLake table.rulake.json bundle witnesses."
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.11"
authors = [{ name = "ruLake Python examples" }]
license = { text = "Apache-2.0 OR MIT" }
keywords = ["rulake", "vector-cache", "shake-256", "bundle", "witness"]

# Pure-stdlib runtime: hashlib.shake_256 covers SHAKE-256(32). No
# third-party crypto needed at runtime; this is by design so an
# operator can drop the verifier into any 3.11+ image.
dependencies = []

[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = ["pytest>=7.4", "mypy>=1.8"]

[project.scripts]
rulake-verify-witness = "verify_witness:main"

[tool.setuptools]
py-modules = ["rulake_witness", "verify_witness"]

[tool.mypy]
strict = true
python_version = "3.11"

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
title: pyproject.toml

Config sdk/python/pyproject.toml:
# ruLake Python SDK — PEP 517 build via maturin (ADR-002).
#
# Build a wheel:    maturin build --release
# Build + install:  maturin develop --release
# Build sdist:      maturin sdist
# Run tests:        pytest tests/

[build-system]
requires = ["maturin>=1.5,<2.0"]
build-backend = "maturin"

[project]
name = "rulake"
version = "2.3.0-alpha.1"
description = "Memory Lake for Agentic AI — fast, witness-anchored vector memory for LLM agents. Cache layer for RAG, semantic search, federated retrieval over S3/BigQuery/Parquet, MCP-compatible. Python bindings."
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.9"
license = { text = "MIT OR Apache-2.0" }
authors = [{ name = "Ruvector Team" }]
keywords = [
    "ai", "agent", "agentic", "agent-memory",
    "llm", "rag", "retrieval-augmented-generation",
    "vector", "vector-search", "vector-database", "semantic-search",
    "embedding", "embeddings", "embedding-cache",
    "ann", "approximate-nearest-neighbor",
    "rabitq", "quantization", "cache", "memory",
    "datalake", "lakehouse", "federation",
    "mcp", "model-context-protocol", "claude", "anthropic", "openai",
    "langchain", "llamaindex",
    "provenance", "witness", "edge-ai",
    "rust", "pyo3", "ruvector",
]
classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 4 - Beta",
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
    "Intended Audience :: Science/Research",
    "Programming Language :: Rust",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.9",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.10",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
    "License :: OSI Approved :: MIT License",
    "License :: OSI Approved :: Apache Software License",
    "Operating System :: OS Independent",
    "Topic :: Database",
    "Topic :: Scientific/Engineering :: Artificial Intelligence",
    "Topic :: Scientific/Engineering :: Information Analysis",
    "Topic :: Software Development :: Libraries :: Python Modules",
    "Typing :: Typed",
]
dependencies = [
    "numpy>=1.21",
]

[project.urls]
Homepage   = "https://github.com/ruvnet/RuLake"
Repository = "https://github.com/ruvnet/RuLake"
Issues     = "https://github.com/ruvnet/RuLake/issues"

[project.optional-dependencies]
test = ["pytest>=7", "pytest-asyncio>=0.21"]

[tool.maturin]
# The native module's import name. The pure-Python wrapper at
# python_src/rulake/__init__.py re-exports from rulake._rulake.
module-name = "rulake._rulake"
features = ["pyo3/extension-module"]
# Pure-Python source tree shipped alongside the .so/.pyd. Holds the
# user-facing __init__.py, type stubs, and py.typed marker.
python-source = "python_src"

# sdist must include the parent crate sources (path-dep) and the
# vendored rabitq submodule the parent depends on. Without these
# `pip install <sdist>` cannot build in an air-gapped environment.
include = [
    { path = "../../crates/core/src/**/*.rs",                      format = "sdist" },
    { path = "../../crates/core/Cargo.toml",                       format = "sdist" },
    { path = "../../crates/core/Cargo.lock",                       format = "sdist" },
    { path = "../../vendor/ruvector/Cargo.toml",                   format = "sdist" },
    { path = "../../vendor/ruvector/Cargo.lock",                   format = "sdist" },
    { path = "../../vendor/ruvector/crates/ruvector-rabitq/**/*",  format = "sdist" },
]
title: pyproject.toml
